messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: http://ryantoussaint.com/projects/tests/microfluidics/doc/Srinivasan1.2004.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1117/12.580145

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidic Protein Droplet Stamping for MALDI Mass Spectrometry (Oil-Encased Droplet Transport, Passive Stamping, and MALDI-TOF Analysis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Protein Sample (bovine serum albumin (BSA) test solutions at 0.001-10 mg/mL, and the ABI 4700 proteomics analyzer calibration mixture containing des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39), and ACTH (7-38) in alpha-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid/acetonitrile/TFA matrix)
  - Silicone Oil (1 cSt filler/encasing medium that immerses droplets to prevent evaporation, minimize non-specific protein adsorption to the Teflon AF surface, and facilitate electrowetting transport)

STEPS:
1. Reservoir loading: Inject the protein sample into the on-chip reservoir, either from a well-plate via syringe-pump pressure (for water/low-viscosity samples) or by pipette (for protein solutions), with the reservoir and droplets immersed in silicone oil.
2. Droplet formation: Generate a unit droplet (~40 nL, electrode pitch L=750 um, spacer thickness H~75 um) from the reservoir using purely internal electrowetting forces, reliable up to 0.01 mg/mL BSA.
3. Transport: Actuate the oil-encased droplet across the electrode array toward the stamping hole; the silicone oil film isolates the droplet from the hydrophobic Teflon AF surface, minimizing irreversible protein adsorption and enabling transport of BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL.
4. Passive stamping: Route the droplet to the stamping hole (diameter >> spacer thickness) and vertically stamp it through the polycarbonate top plate onto the target substrate (hydrophobic glass slide with hydrophilic patch, or a standard MALDI target plate), where the larger hole diameter passively forces the droplet out without active pressure, leaving some liquid behind as dead volume.
5. MALDI-MS analysis: Analyze the stamped droplet(s) on a MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer (e.g. ABI 4700 MALDI-MS TOF system) to acquire the mass spectrum and confirm protein identity and relative intensity.
6. Cycle repeat: Repeat droplet formation, transport, and stamping for additional droplets to increase the total amount of protein deposited at the stamping site (e.g. 10 droplets dispensed, 6 stamped, 4 left as dead volume in one reported run).

INTERPRETATION: Successful protein stamping is confirmed by droplet transport being demonstrated for BSA concentrations up to 10 mg/mL (three orders of magnitude higher than prior electrowetting protein-handling reports) and reliable electrowetting-only droplet formation up to 0.01 mg/mL, by passive stamping depositing quantifiable protein amounts onto a target substrate (3.6 fmoles from 0.001 mg/mL and 16 fmoles from 0.01 mg/mL BSA solutions), and by MALDI-TOF mass spectra of the stamped ABI 4700 calibration mixture correctly identifying all constituent proteins (des-Arg-Bradykinin, Angiotensin I, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B, ACTH (1-17), ACTH (18-39)) after on-chip transport and stamping, establishing the feasibility of a compact, fast, moving-part-free electrowetting interface between well-plate sample formats and MALDI-MS target substrates.

source.title: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidic Protein Droplet Stamping for MALDI Mass Spectrometry (Oil-Encased Droplet Transport, Passive Stamping, and MALDI-TOF Analysis)

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA, A-4378) was obtained from Sigma Chemicals ... and stock solutions of 0.1mg/mL, 0.01mg/mL and 0.001mg/mL were prepared in de-ionized water
1cSt silicone oil (DMS-T01, Gelest, Morrisville, Pennsylvania, USA) is used as the filler medium surrounding the droplets to prevent evaporation and facilitate transport

operation_evidence.bs_operation: sample = dispense Protein_Sample / encased = mix sample with oil for 5s
operation_evidence.source_quote: Droplet formation using only electrowetting forces is tested for BSA solutions with concentrations ranging from 0.001-0.1mg/mL

operation_evidence.bs_operation: transported = mix encased with oil for 2s
operation_evidence.source_quote: Droplets are then automatically generated from the reservoir, routed to the stamping hole, and vertically stamped onto the stamping target

operation_evidence.bs_operation: stamped = mix transported with oil for 1s
operation_evidence.source_quote: the liquid is passively pushed out of the stamping hole ... which forces the droplet out spontaneously without active forces

operation_evidence.bs_operation: spectrum = detect fluorescence on stamped for 10s
operation_evidence.source_quote: The MALDI plate was then analyzed on an ABI4700 MALDI TOF/TOF system and the spectrum obtained is shown in Figure 5
operation_evidence.source_location: Section 5.4, MALDI-MS on protein calibration solution

operation_evidence.source_quote: 10 droplets (~40nl each) of 0.001mg/mL were dispensed from the reservoir, of which 6 droplets (~240nL corresponding to 3.6fmoles) was stamped onto the glass slide

numeric_mismatches.note: Stands in for the paper's reported example of 6 successfully stamped droplets out of 10 dispensed (Section 5.3, Fig. 4); the paper does not itself describe this as a fixed instruction-repeat count, since droplet count depends on the specific experiment (10 droplets in one run, 2 droplets of ABI 4700 calibration solution in another, Section 5.4).

numeric_mismatches.field: transported = mix encased with oil for 2s / stamped = mix transported with oil for 1s
numeric_mismatches.note: Electrowetting transport and passive gravity/pressure-driven stamping-hole ejection are physical droplet-movement operations with no exact BioScript primitive; they are approximated here as short 'mix' operations with silicone oil (durations illustrative) rather than literal chemical mixing steps, since the paper does not report explicit timings for these movements.

numeric_mismatches.field: spectrum = detect fluorescence on stamped for 10s
numeric_mismatches.note: 'fluorescence' stands in for the paper's actual MALDI-TOF mass spectrum acquisition on an ABI 4700 system; the 10s duration is illustrative since the paper does not report a specific per-droplet MS acquisition time.

numeric_mismatches.field: switching-frequency-vs-voltage characterization (Fig. 3), formation/transport concentration limits (Sections 5.1-5.2), well-plate interface hardware (Fig. 2), mass-spectrum peak assignments (Fig. 5)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are device-characterization measurements, hardware/interface design description, and downstream mass-spectrum peak analysis rather than steps of the core dispense/transport/stamp/detect protocol itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidic Protein Droplet Stamping for MALDI Mass Spectrometry (Oil-Encased Droplet Transport, Passive Stamping, and MALDI-TOF Analysis). The assay is performed on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Protein Sample and Silicone Oil.
